blocks.h2: Is Your Algonquin Sewer Line Damaged?
blocks.intro: Clogs clear. Damage keeps coming back. Look for:

tiles.h3: Repeat Clogs at the Same Spot
tiles.body: If the main line keeps blocking at the same distance from the house, something there is catching debris: roots, a sag or a broken joint.
When the washer or a toilet upstairs drains, gurgling at the floor drain means the line is partly blocked.

tiles.h3: Slow Drains That Cleaning Doesn't Fix
tiles.body: If professional cleaning only helps for a few weeks, the pipe itself has a problem.
Cracks, offset joints, roots or a belly in the line mean it's time to talk repair.

blocks.h2: Why Sewer Lines Fail in Algonquin
blocks.intro: The median home in Algonquin was built in 1994, and more than half went up between 1990 and 2009. The lines are younger than in older suburbs, but they're reaching the age when problems show up.

items.h3: Subdivision Trees Are Now Full Grown
items.body: Trees planted when Algonquin's subdivisions went in are now 17 to 36 years old. Their roots reach farther every year and find any joint that lets moisture out.
Sewer trenches were backfilled when each subdivision was built, and soil keeps settling for years. A section that settled unevenly becomes a sag that holds water and paper.
Homes closer to the Fox River and the older part of town may have clay or cast iron lines with the usual age-related problems.
With 88% of homes owner-occupied and lots of families, lines carry a lot of grease, wipes and paper. That speeds up any weakness in the pipe.

blocks.h2: How We Repair Sewer Lines in Algonquin
blocks.intro: From our Esplanade Drive office, every sewer repair follows the same three steps.

steps.body: We camera the line from the cleanout to the main and record every problem with its distance and depth.

steps.h3: 2. Pick the Smallest Fix That Works
steps.body: A spot repair for one bad section, lining or replacement for a failing line. You see the footage that backs it up.
You get a flat-rate price, in writing, before we start.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: Algonquin yards often have patios, sprinkler systems and mature landscaping over the sewer path. The camera tells us which method keeps the most of it intact.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: My house was built in the 1990s. Why does it need sewer work already?
items.preview: Roots from maturing trees and settled soil are the usual reasons.
items.answer: Pipe from the 1990s isn't old, but the trees around it are now big enough to send roots into joints, and the soil has had decades to settle. Either can cause repeat clogs. The camera shows which.

items.q: Can you fix just the bad section?
items.preview: Often, yes. A spot repair is cheaper when the rest of the line is sound.
items.answer: Often, yes. If the camera shows one sag or broken joint and the rest is in good shape, we repair just that section. If problems run the length of the line, [lining or replacement](/algonquin/trenchless-sewer-repair) makes more sense.

items.q: Will a sewer repair ruin my lawn and sprinklers?
items.preview: Trenchless methods keep most of the yard intact. We mark sprinkler lines before we dig.
items.answer: Trenchless methods need only small openings. When digging is needed, we work around sprinkler lines and landscaping and restore the area we open.

items.q: Whose responsibility is the sewer line?
items.preview: Usually yours, from the house to the main.
items.answer: Usually the homeowner's, from the house to the connection at the public main. If the camera shows the problem is in the main, we'll let you know.

items.q: What does sewer line repair cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: That depends on what the camera finds. You'll see a flat price first.
items.answer: It comes down to what the camera shows: the type of damage, how deep and long the bad section is, the method and what's above it. You'll have a flat-rate number in hand before work starts.
